newsitem.title: UK: Syria insists on Dtd -55 cts July crude offer - trade.
newsitem.headline: Syria insists on Dtd -55 cts July crude offer - trade.

text.p: Syria has insisted on its opening offer of Dated Brent -55 for its Syrian Light crude for July desite bearish news suggesting an early resumption if Iraq exports, traders said on Wednesday.
State-owned Sytrol apparently feels confident about obtaining a firm price because of market scepticism about Iraq stateted intention to resume exports in seven to 10 days' time, the traders said.
Traders continue to assess the Mediterranean sour market as buoyant in the near term and supportive also of the lighter grades.

Sytrol's customers had resisted the offer, a 22 cents increase from June, for fear that a possible resumption of Iraqi exports would send spot prices tumbling. Most opening bids were for a rollover at Dated -77 cents.
They pointed to an Iraqi statement in Vienna on Tuesday that Baghdad would start exporting oil again once the "oil-for-food" aid distribution plan had been finalised in seven to 10 days.
But political and logistical hurdles in the way of renewed sales are sufficiently numerous for most traders to predict a resumption of exports only in mid- to late July at the earliest.
